candidates.changed_node: removed the whole modulator product CS_RANK(MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 0)) * CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42)) and the redundant CS_DEMEAN wrapper, replacing it with a single CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 42)) risk leg - drops $leverage, $volume, $high, $low and the 0 constant
candidates.rationale: Parent is quality minus a two-part turbulence modulator (rising leverage x volume/range comovement); both parts proxy the same thing, so they collapse into one realised-vol penalty. Cost 5 fields + 1 const + depth 5 = 11 -> 2 + 0 + 3 = 5. IC floor is 0.00901 and a two-rank spread scores ~0.707*(IC_a+IC_b): the $roe rank leg back-solves to ~0.0080 (from CS_RANK($roe)-CS_RANK($volume) 0.01188 with $volume 0.00881) and a return-vol leg to ~0.0110 (the roe/TS_STD($return,10) spread scored 0.01348 before it was evicted), so this lands ~0.013, comfortably clear. Window 42 rather than 10 keeps the leg as slow as the parent (41-day IC half-life, 0.033 turnover) and dodges the evicted variant. Structurally free: no live member uses TS_STD($return, 42) (5/15/21/63/105/126 are in play) and Alpha101 uses 2/5/20, so nothing shares 4 nodes; CS_RANK($roe) is 2 nodes. Keeping the corr kernel was not available - dropping only the leverage modulator reproduces the already-accepted sibling CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) - CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high-$low, 15)), and near variants of it drew 0.853-0.900 correlation rejects.

candidates.changed_node: removed the range modulator - the CS_ZSCORE(...) * CS_RANK(($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8)) product becomes a plain rank spread, and the CS_DEMEAN wrapper goes with it; the leverage penalty survives at the 126-day horizon
candidates.rationale: Parent is quality minus (z-scored leverage growth x relative intraday range). The range term is the price half of the modulator; removing it leaves the quality-vs-rising-leverage spread the parent is built on. Cost 5 fields + 0 consts + depth 6 = 11 -> 2 + 0 + 3 = 5, dropping $high, $low, $open and three levels of depth. CS_ZSCORE has roughly 3x the cross-sectional dispersion of a rank, so the parent's variance is dominated by the leverage x range product and this child sits far from it rather than on top of it. The leverage leg moves to the 126-day delta because every 63-day wrapper (CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE, ABS, MAX(.,0), unary minus) is already a 4-node live-archive block; TS_DELTA($leverage, 126) appears live only under CS_ZSCORE, so CS_RANK of it is a distinct tree sharing just 3 nodes, and 126 days spans two report stamps so the delta is not mostly zeros. IC floor is 0.00652: back-solving (CS_RANK($roe)-CS_RANK($leverage))-CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage,63)) = 0.00771 puts a leverage-delta rank near 0.0027 against ~0.0080 for the roe rank, so the spread lands ~0.0075.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: SIMPLIFY. Each expression below was flagged as more complex than it needs
to be. Return a simpler expression that keeps the same idea.

Simpler means strictly fewer distinct fields, fewer free constants, or less
depth. The simplification is accepted only if it also keeps at least
80% of the parent's fit-window |IC|, so do not remove the component
doing the work. Put the parent's id in `parent_ids` and name what you removed in
`changed_node`.
